notes: Ran the tests the runner could not: disposable PG17 + pgcrypto in igame_test_extensions, all 4 new tests PASS; internal/api (28.8s) + internal/database green with DSN; go test ./... without DSN green; gofmt/go vet/go build clean; worktree clean afterwards.

Mutation-verified that the tests pin real behavior, not just compile: (M1) deleting `p.Permissions = effectiveKeyPermissions(...)` in api.go:453 -> TestAPIKeyScopeFollowsPolicyWithoutReissuingTheKey fails at apikey_scope_pg_test.go:173 (200, want 403 insufficient_scope); (M2) deleting the `/api-keys` refusal at api.go:543-546 -> TestAPIKeyCannotManageAPIKeys fails on GET (200) and on rotate (201 with a fresh secret); (M3) dropping `revoked_at IS NULL AND (expires_at IS NULL OR expires_at>now())` from authenticateAPIKey -> all three lifecycle subtests fail (200, want 401).

Implementer's self-doubt (b) is confirmed true and should not be overstated in release notes: TestAPIKeyLosesAdminReachWhenOwnerIsDemoted stayed GREEN under mutation M1, because requireRole (api.go:466) already 403s on role='user' alone. That test pins the outcome, not the policy-reload mechanism; TestAPIKeyScopeFollowsPolicyWithoutReissuingTheKey is the only one that pins the reload.

Self-doubt (c) is resolved, not a flake: putSetting calls s.invalidateSetting(key) (admin.go:166) and settingFixture reuses the same Server instance via f.settings(), so the 5s settingsTTL never applies. Multi-instance staleness stays out of scope, as the cache comment already says.

Weakest of the four: the POST /api/v1/me/api-keys subtest. With the guard removed it fails on `invalid_json` (empty body) rather than reaching createAPIKey, so it pins 'refused' but not 'refused before a well-formed create'. The GET and rotate subtests carry the actual escalation signal.

Pre-existing and unchanged, deliberately left by the implementer and correctly so: loadAPIKeyPolicyContext propagating ErrNoRows when the api_keys row is absent (fail-closed 401 for every key — availability, not an auth bypass), and the `touched` CTE bumping last_used_at on already-expired keys. Neither is introduced here; the README sentence added claims only that rotation/revoke/expiry cut authentication, which is accurate.

Security: no production code changed (test + one README sentence only), no new endpoint, no new dependency, no secret handling, no migration, no widening of any role. Legal/privacy: fixtures insert synthetic users (uuid usernames, literal 'old-hash') into a throwaway schema; no personal data is collected, stored, or transmitted, and no production data is loaded into the test environment.

Coverage caveat for the next round: CI `make test` sets no IGAME_TEST_DSN, so these four tests never run in CI — the regression only protects whoever runs `make test-db`. Consistent with every existing *_pg_test.go, so not a blocker, but the release note should not imply CI enforces it. Revert cost is one file delete plus one README sentence.
